newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya raises minimum investment in T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Kenya raises minimum investment in T-bills.

text.p: The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) said on Tuesday it would raise the minimum investment in government treasury bills to one million shillings ($17,857) from 50,000 shilllings ($892) with effect from January 1, 1997.

"The action will not only reduce administrative paperwork at the Central Bank of Kenya, but is in line with worldwide central banks' practice of dealing in the wholesale money markets," CBK Chief Banking Manager Reuben Marambii said in a statement.
"The retail end of the market will be left to commercial banks," Marambii added.

Marambii said investors of amounts below 1,000,000 shillings averaged 53.2 percent of total applicants but only 0.63 percent of the total value. The bank's main category of treasury bills are 28-day, 91-day, and 182-day.
